page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with a decorative ornament band above the heading. No margin notes. Below the heading, the numbered theses are set one per paragraph. Faint mirrored show-through text from the reverse side is ignored.

main_text.head: PARADOXA.
main_text.p: Professores Philosophiæ docent Philosophiam quam non habent, & habent Philosophiam quam non docent.
II. Logica unica hora perfectè doceri potest.
III. Logica non potest dirigere operationes mentis.
IV. Omne genus, & omnis species formaliter est individuum: & species est species non est propositio identica.
V. Omnis enunciatio potest esse vera: & in hac, hoc est corpus meum, corpus meum non est prædicatum.
VI. Paternitas & filiatio non distinguuntur realiter.
VII. Aristoteles nullas agnovit formas substantiales.
IX. In unica hebdomade tres dies Iovis esse possunt in eadem urbe.
X. Corpora rarefacta non habent plus extensionis quàm den-sata.

page.notes: The Roman numerals I to X are set above each thesis in the printed page. The word "perfectè" is printed with an accent that is hard to make out; I read it as perfectè [?]. The "h" and "a" of "habent" in thesis I are clear. The ornament band at the top is not transcribed. The "33" at the top right is taken as the page number. The mirrored text at the top and in the background is show-through and was left out. The large initial "P" of the first paragraph is joined to "Professores" as one word.
